fields.features_heading: What Each Signed Consent Should Record
fields.features_subheading: A signature line proves someone agreed. The app Emergent builds also keeps which test it was, why it ran, and who sees the result.
fields.feature_1:
The test and its reason, picked from a list

The signer sees which test it is before signing: urine or oral fluid, and pre-employment, random, post-accident, or reasonable suspicion. Both picks are saved with the signature.
fields.feature_2:
An e-signature from the signer's phone

Applicants open the consent from an emailed link and sign with a finger on the screen. The app saves the typed name, the date, and the signature in one record you can search.
fields.feature_3:
A release naming who receives the result

List the people or roles allowed to receive the result inside the consent itself, such as one HR manager. The signer reads that list before signing, and it stays on the record.
fields.feature_4:
Signed counts for a random testing pool

See how many employees in the pool have signed and which have not. The app emails a reminder on the schedule you set, and each new signature takes a name off the unsigned list.
fields.feature_5:
A second signature for applicants under 18

When the birth date shows an applicant is under 18, the form asks a parent or guardian to sign too. The record stays open until both signatures are in, and HR sees which is missing.
fields.feature_6:
Consent records you can take with you

On paid plans, export the full codebase to your GitHub repository and host the consent app alongside your other HR systems. Every signed consent stays in a database you own.

fields.tab_content_1:
Leni signs from her phone and tests within 48 hours

Copper Flats Cold Storage emails a conditional offer to warehouse applicant Leni Harlan with a link to the consent. She signs on her phone and picks a collection site near her. HR sees the signed form and a 48-hour window to test, and her start date waits on the result.
fields.tab_content_2:
Reminders every 3 days until all 186 have signed

Brookfield Molding keeps 186 plant employees in its random testing pool, and each one signs the consent and the policy acknowledgment once. Right now 171 of the 186 have signed. The 15 who have not get an email reminder every 3 days, and the plant manager sees their names on one list.
fields.tab_content_3:
For the post-accident result, one named reader

A forklift backs into a racking upright at Wren Mills Lumber. The shift supervisor opens the post-accident form on a tablet, picks the test reason, and hands it to the operator to sign. The release on that form names Joanne Pike in HR as the only person who receives the result.
fields.tab_content_4:
Consent for 23 dock hires, none for 9 drivers

Kettle River Freight hired 9 drivers and 23 dock workers in one week. DOT rules bar an employer from requiring a signed consent for the testing they cover. The form skips the consent page for the DOT-covered driver roles. The 23 dock hires see the page and sign it.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Drug Test Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a drug test consent form that skips DOT-covered roles, names who sees results, and gets signed on a phone.
fields.howto_step_1_des: DOT rules say DOT tests must be completely separate from non-DOT tests in all respects, and every DOT collection is documented on the federal custody and control form. List which roles fall under DOT rules; the consent form goes only to the other roles.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask your employment counsel to set the consent wording before the form goes live. Paste the approved text into your prompt word for word, and keep each version to show which one an employee signed.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write down each specimen you collect, such as urine or oral fluid, and every reason your written policy gives for testing someone. These become the two lists the signer picks from before the signature line appears.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide which people or roles receive a result for each test reason, and keep the list short. A post-accident result might go to one HR manager and nobody else. The form shows that list above the signature line.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Pick the moment each form goes out
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tie each form to the moment it is needed: a conditional offer for applicants, enrollment for a random pool, an incident for post-accident tests. The app emails the link at that point and reminds anyone who has not signed.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write a prompt that names the roles that sign and the reasons you test. Emergent builds the form with an e-signature step and a database behind it, and you change any part later by asking in plain English.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the first applicant sees it, sign a test consent on your own phone for each test reason. Check that the approved wording appears, the recipient list is right, and the signed record lands where HR will look for it.

faq_plan.q: What is a drug test consent form?
faq_plan.ref: What is a drug test consent form?

prov.original: What is a drug test consent form?

faq_plan.a: A drug test consent form records that an applicant or employee agreed to take a drug test. A complete one names the specimen, the reason for the test, and the people who may receive the result. It closes with a dated signature.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a drug test consent form?
faq_plan.a: Settle the test reasons and who may receive results, and get the consent wording from your employment counsel. Then describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the signing flow and stores each signed consent in a database you own. Ask for changes the same way, in plain English.

faq_plan.q: What should a drug testing consent form for employees include?
faq_plan.a: Include the signer's name and role, the specimen type, why the test was ordered, and the collection site. Then add the people allowed to receive the result and the consent wording your employment counsel approves. End with the e-signature and the date. Give the policy acknowledgment its own checkbox, and each answer is recorded on its own.

faq_plan.q: Should a pre-employment drug test consent form be part of the job application?
faq_plan.a: Keep it separate. A job application form goes to everyone who applies, while the consent goes only to the applicants you decide to test, at the point in hiring your employment counsel sets. A separate form also keeps the signature and the test window on their own record.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a drug test consent form for federally regulated transportation jobs?
faq_plan.a: Not for tests under the DOT program. Under 49 CFR 40.27, an employer must not require an employee to sign a consent, release, waiver of liability, or indemnification agreement for any part of the testing process Part 40 covers. A consent form belongs to tests outside that program, and your counsel can confirm which roles fall under it.

faq_plan.q: How is a drug test consent form different from a custody and control form?
faq_plan.a: The consent form is the employer's own record that a person agreed to a test. The Federal Drug Testing Custody and Control Form documents the collection itself. Under 49 CFR 40.40, it must be used for every collection the DOT drug testing program requires, and a non-Federal form must not be used to conduct one.

faq_plan.q: How do I collect a random drug test consent form from every employee in the pool?
faq_plan.a: Send each employee in the pool one link to sign, then let the app track who has not. It sends an email reminder at the interval you pick and keeps the unsigned names on one list for the person who runs the pool. Emergent builds that reminder logic from a plain-English prompt, with no response caps.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free drug test consent form employees can sign online?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing. Employees open the consent on a phone or a computer and sign it with an e-signature, and each signed form is saved as its own record in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should a drug test consent form also cover alcohol testing?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if you test for both. A drug and alcohol consent form with a separate checkbox for each test shows exactly what the person agreed to, test by test. Your employment counsel decides whether both belong under one signature.

faq_plan.q: What happens after an applicant signs the drug test consent form?
faq_plan.a: The applicant gets an email with the collection site and the deadline to test, and HR sees the signed consent with the date it was signed. Once the result is back and the hire goes ahead, the next step is the new employee form for payroll and start-date details.

plan.angle: The top 10 is fixed documents: state workforce agency samples (Texas, Tennessee), hospital occupational-health PDFs, a parental consent PDF, a university HR form and SHRM, J.J. Keller and HR.com templates. Each is one paragraph of consent and a signature line, and none says where a consent form does not belong: 49 CFR 40.27 bars an employer from requiring a consent for testing covered by Part 40, and every DOT collection runs on the federal custody and control form. This page draws that line first, then builds what a PDF cannot: an e-signature on a phone, a release that names who receives the result, a signed count for a random pool, and logic that shows the consent page only to roles outside the DOT program.
